parts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: isolated reference for one modular realistic medieval RPG upper-body armor, for image-to-3D reconstruction. Make a practical starter knight steel plate cuirass with integrated rounded pauldrons, articulated upper-arm and forearm armor, small elbow cops, overlapping waist lames ending at the hips. Matching set design: satin silver forged steel, subtle rolled steel edges, restrained dark steel rivets, charcoal padded fabric only at flexible joints, a few dark brown fastening straps; no gold, no ornament, no heraldry. Athletic adult male proportions, regular build, not bulky. Hollow empty garment in a symmetrical neutral T-pose, both arms extended perfectly horizontal, wrists open and empty, neck open, no hands, no head, no person, no mannequin, no legs. Direct front view, near orthographic, full object centered and filling image with generous margin around arm ends. Uniform pale gray background, clean softly lit game asset render with readable separate plates, physically plausible steel highlights, no cast shadow, no text, no panels, no weapons, no additional objects. The garment must have sleeves and both arms from shoulders through forearms, but no gloves.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: isolated modular medieval RPG armor reference for image-to-3D reconstruction. Design matches the reference upper-body armor exactly in material language: satin silver forged steel, subtle rolled edges, small dark steel rivets, charcoal quilted fabric at flexible joints, dark brown fastening straps, no gold, no heraldry, no ornament. The input image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, do not include the cuirass or arms in the output. Clean softly lit realistic game asset render, uniform pale gray backdrop, one single view, no people, mannequin, human skin, labels, text, panels or extra objects. Primary request: one hollow pair of armored trousers for an athletic adult male, waist through ankles, front view near orthographic. Complete connected trousers with a narrow charcoal waistband and flexible charcoal crotch, silver steel articulated cuisses covering thighs, rounded knee cops, narrow articulated calf plates. Legs straight and slightly separated at the ankles, left-right symmetric, natural proportions. No feet, boots, torso or belt ornaments. Centered, whole garment visible, 10% empty margin. Functional starter knight design with clearly readable metal thigh and knee plates, not fabric trousers.

Match the reference armor's material and style: satin silver forged steel, subtle rolled edges, small dark steel rivets, charcoal padded fabric at joints and dark brown fastening straps. Both feet parallel, heels side by side with clear separation, toes pointing toward viewer. Front three-quarter view slightly above the feet shows each segmented instep and articulated rounded toe, black leather sole and short ankle cuff. Hollow openings visible at top, no leg inside. Realistic practical medieval footwear, modest width, no exaggerated pointed toes. Complete disconnected left and right boots only, no trousers, legs, hands or gauntlets.

Exactly one glove; its partner will be mirrored in 3D.

unused_meshy.usage: Unused: rough upper-body surface; replaced with 4K geometry generation.

processing.method: Fit to original 65-bone A pose, adjust gorget and wrist openings, align knees/ankles, fit five finger landmarks and mirror gauntlet; transfer body weights, rigid Head binding for helmet. Smooth normals, rebuild tangent space, compact GLB data, compress runtime textures. No geometry decimation after generation.
processing.licenses: Inherited from original modular body/Mixamo and the Meshy paid-generation terms recorded above; local fitting adds no third-party asset.

ankle_correction.method: Recenter boot cuffs on each shin bone axis; taper greave ends inside the cuffs; use the same height-based Leg/Foot blend over both ankle overlaps. Preserve toes, soles and triangle counts.
ankle_correction.visual_review: Both ankles from front and rear: idle, combat idle, two walking phases, running and jumping.

wrist_correction.method: Center and taper distal vambraces on each ForeArm–Hand axis. Align and flare gauntlet cuffs around that axis, blending back into the existing palm warp. Use the same axial-distance ForeArm/Hand weight profile throughout the overlap.

wrist_cuff_rebuild.method: Remove three nonmanifold source flaps per hand, clip the old cuff at source Z = -0.5, stitch its ordered boundary to an elliptical steel cuff with a beveled rim, and close the inside with a recessed padded lining. Mirror the completed geometry and retain the shared ForeArm/Hand weights. Store part metadata on the mesh as well as its node for multi-material loading.

visual_review.views: Side views and oblique views looking into both cuff openings

ankle_overlap_rebuild.reference: User-provided photograph of greaves overlapping sabatons, supplied in conversation; used for shape reference only, not copied into textures or distributed assets.
ankle_overlap_rebuild.method: Replace the tucked greave taper with an outer shell: raise the front hem into an arch, extend the sides and rear downward, and narrow the sabaton cuff on the shin axis. Subdivide only long source edges near the greave hems, interpolate UVs, and retain the shared height-based Leg/Foot weight profile.
preserved: Boot toe and sole geometry below 85 mm

arch_centering.reason: The arch was centered on the shin bone while the fitted sabaton instep ridge lies farther outward.
arch_centering.method: Offset only the front arch center 14 mm outward on each side to align it with the visible instep ridge; retain the rear hem profile, upper greave geometry, UVs, topology and boot mesh.

visual_review.views: Looking down the toe direction of each foot

crotch_weight_correction.cause: Nearest-body vertex weight transfer assigned adjacent central gusset vertices strongly to opposite thighs, stretching their shared faces during wide leg poses.
crotch_weight_correction.method: Replace front crotch weights with a continuous height-dependent Hips/LeftUpLeg/RightUpLeg field and blend back to the original weights at the region boundary. Widen the thigh transition toward the pelvis. Fade the correction from Z = -0.04 to 0.01 m to preserve rear armor weights.
preserved: Ankle shape, weights and arch centering
Weights outside the crotch region within 1e-7
Rear armor weights at Z <= -0.04 m within 1e-7

deformation_comparison.metric: Maximum deformed/rest edge-length ratio per sampled triangle; not a claim of zero deformation.
deformation_comparison.triangle_selection: Rest-pose face centroid: 0.72 <= Y < 1.02 m, abs(X) <= 0.19 m and Z > 0.01 m

helmet_width_correction.method: Reduce lateral width by 15% away from the ears. Smoothly blend the ear region to X = sign(X) * (0.101 + (abs(X) - 0.10) * 0.3) m using the pre-correction fitted coordinates, keeping the shell close to the ears without the penetration caused by uniform scaling. Rebuild normals and tangents.
preserved: 65-bone rig, rigid Head weights and animations

helmet_bevor_addition.source: Locally authored procedural geometry and steel PBR material in tools/fit-modular-plate.py; no external asset or generated texture added.
helmet_bevor_addition.method: Add a closed curved lower-face plate from below the nose to the chin, with a shallow center ridge, beveled rim and ends overlapping the existing cheek guards. Bind it rigidly to Head and store part metadata on the mesh for loading both material primitives together.
preserved: Previously narrowed helmet shell, normals, tangents and UVs
helmet_bevor_addition.usage: Unused: the separate 272-triangle guard and Steel bevor material were removed at the user's request.

helmet_cheek_wrap.reference: User-annotated side view identifying the original cheek guard; used as the shape-edit reference.
helmet_cheek_wrap.method: Remove the separate mouth guard and its material. Lengthen the original left and right cheek guards along a curved path toward the mouth, curl the lower tips upward toward the chin, and blend into the existing narrowed upper helmet. Subdivide source edges only where curved midpoints deviate by more than 3 mm, with at most three passes; interpolate original UVs and rebuild normals/tangents.
preserved: Original Meshy PBR image bytes and material
Original UV vertices, with interpolated UVs on subdivided edges
65-bone rig, rigid Head weights and animations

visual_review.comparison: Previous separate guard versus extended original cheek guards

helmet_neck_closure.reference: User-provided low-angle game screenshot showing exposed skin below the chin, followed by two closed-helmet photographs; shape references only.
helmet_neck_closure.method: Continue the existing cheek guards beneath the chin into a rounded throat. Blend their lower vertices toward an elliptical neck opening centered at Z = -0.042 m, preserve radial thickness, and tuck the lower hem inside the existing gorget. Retain the original helmet material and extend only its source geometry; no separate plate or material is added. Subdivide curved source edges and interpolate original UVs.
preserved: Helmet shape at and above Y = 1.70 m
Original PBR images, material and existing UV vertices
Other armor parts and animation files

bare_waist_clearance.cause: The front belt and padded trouser waist intersected the visible lower torso when no top was equipped.
bare_waist_clearance.source: Local fit adjustment of the existing Meshy plate geometry; licenses unchanged.
bare_waist_clearance.method: Offset the front waist in +Z by up to 16mm. Apply the same smooth field to the overlapping plate cuirass waist to preserve its overlap. Rebuild normals/tangents and transfer skin weights at the adjusted positions.
bare_waist_clearance.deformation: z += 0.016 * smoothstep(0.99, 1.06, y) * (1 - smoothstep(1.15, 1.24, y)) * (1 - smoothstep(0.10, 0.17, abs(x))) * smoothstep(0.015, 0.060, z)
preserved: geometry and skin weights outside the adjusted waist

ankle_collar_width.source: Local refit of existing plate boots and pants for anatomical ankle width; original license records apply. No AI generation or credits.
ankle_collar_width.pants_followup: The boot enlargement remains; plate_cuff_close_fit reduces the resulting trouser-hem flare without resizing boots.

plate_cuff_close_fit.purpose: Reduce the enlarged plate trouser hem flare and fit it closer over the unchanged plate boots, including the view from below.
plate_cuff_close_fit.source: Local refit of existing plate pants; original Meshy and Mixamo license records apply.
plate_cuff_close_fit.tool: NumPy mesh deformation, Blender source synchronization and existing texture repacker

method.center: Shin axis with the existing boot-collar displacement
method.target: Outermost radial intersection with the corresponding plate boot plus 4 mm; above y = 0.19 m use the y = 0.19 m collar section translated along the shin axis.
method.displacement: Only reduce radius where it exceeds the target. Partial fitting preserves the metal rim and avoids collapsing its folds.
method.normals: Inverse-transpose deformation Jacobian; tangents use the forward Jacobian.
preserved: Geometry at and above y = 0.30 m

arm_body_fit_2026_09_30.request: Match plate-arm position and thickness to the bare body and linen shirt, including barbarian bracers.
arm_body_fit_2026_09_30.method: Fit upper-arm and forearm cross-sections to the existing body along the Arm/ForeArm/Hand axes, with 8 mm clearance and a smooth shoulder transition. Recompute surface normals, tangents and transferred skin weights.
arm_body_fit_2026_09_30.source_and_license: Local edit of the existing Meshy Premium plate source and modular male body; original license records above apply.

validation.minimum_jacobian_scope: Changed arm region (source |x| > 0.30), including vertices and face centers.
